name: Pulmonary arterial hypertension associated with another disease

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: ESC/ERS Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary hypertension

criteria.description: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) ≥ 25 mmHg at rest measured by right heart catheterization
Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) ≤ 15 mmHg to exclude left heart disease
Presence of an associated systemic disease known to cause PAH (e.g., connective tissue disease, HIV infection, portal hypertension)
Exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension such as chronic thromboembolic disease
Echocardiographic evidence of elevated pulmonary artery pressure and right ventricular dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (mPAP ≥ 25 mmHg, PCWP ≤ 15 mmHg, and presence of an associated disease) plus exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Right heart catheterization is mandatory for definitive diagnosis.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fatigue related to reduced cardiac output
searchTerms: fatigue due to low cardiac output

common.symptomName: Peripheral edema due to right heart failure
searchTerms: swelling in legs from heart problems
ankle puffiness due to heart failure

occasional.symptomName: Raynaud phenomenon (if associated with connective tissue disease)
searchTerms: Raynaud's phenomenon with connective tissue disease

rare.symptomName: Hoarseness due to recurrent laryngeal nerve compression
searchTerms: voice changes due to nerve pressure

rare.symptomName: Ascites secondary to right heart failure
searchTerms: fluid buildup in abdomen from heart failure
ascites caused by right heart failure

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP levels
Autoantibodies if associated with connective tissue disease
imaging: Echocardiography showing right ventricular hypertrophy and elevated pulmonary artery pressure
Chest CT or V/Q scan to exclude thromboembolic disease
Right heart catheterization confirming elevated mPAP
genetic: BMPR2 mutations may be present in some cases but less common in associated PAH
other: 6-minute walk test showing reduced exercise capacity
Pulmonary function tests may show reduced diffusing capacity

distinguishingFeatures: V/Q scan showing mismatched perfusion defects

redFlags: Signs of right heart failure such as severe peripheral edema or ascites
references: Galiè N, Humbert M, Vachiery JL, et al. 2015 ESC/ERS Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Heart J. 2016 Jan 1;37(1):67-119.
